notes.title: Railroad Corporation 2 - Out Now in Early Access!
notes.content:
[h2]Great news, everyone! Railroad Corporation 2, the sequel to Railroad Corporation, has been released into Early Access![/h2]

[h3]Check out our Early Access launch trailer below:[/h3]
[previewyoutube=1xH7JmQsctg;full][/previewyoutube]

[u][b]What’s New in Railroad Corporation 2?[/b][/u]

There are already a bunch of features in the launch version of Railroad Corporation 2, and [b]we plan to offer way more as we move through Early Access[/b]. We’ve prepared a [b][i]roadmap [/i][/b]highlighting our plans which is displayed at the bottom of this blog. But for now, let's focus on what’s already in the game.

Building on the foundations of its predecessor, this second edition expands on core features, while also introducing new features for additional strategic depth, including:

[list]
[*][b]Electrification & Expanded Railroad Building:[/b] You can now electrify your tracks, allowing electric locomotives to power through your network. Additionally, new tools have been introduced to refine track laying, including parallel snapping, grid-based placement, and the ability to place tracks over other tracks (also known as diamond crossings).
[*][b]Detailed Locomotive Reports:[/b] Get detailed insights into your locomotives, including statistics about their top speed, max pulling mass, monthly upkeep, and other advanced specifications.
[*][b]Signal Mechanics:[/b] Railroad Corporation 2 introduces signal mechanics to control the flow of traffic and ensure locomotives are running smoothly across junctions.
[*][b]Headquarters & New Departments:[/b] You can choose strategic locations for your headquarters and train stations, and unearth new materials to trade with using the Geology department.
[*][b]Financial & Operational Insights:[/b] Gain a clearer view of your financials with the new reporting tool. This feature provides detailed insights into your company’s activities, a snapshot of how your competitors are doing, and essential market information.[/list]

[u][b]What’s available on Early Access Launch?[/b][/u]
In addition to the expanded core features and new options, you can explore the game through a variety of  game modes, including:

[list]
[*][b]Campaign Story Mode:[/b] Embark on your railroad journey with four initial missions, with new missions being added throughout the Early Access period.
[*][b]Multiplayer Mode:[/b] Test your strategic skills in cooperative or versus scenarios for up to 4 players. Team up with a business partner or face off against others, with distinct maps designed to challenge your strategic prowess among other entrepreneurs.
[*][b]Sandbox Mode:[/b] Unleash your creativity with sandbox mode, allowing you to build and manage your railroad corporation without constraints. With all 10 locomotives unlocked, and all research options completed, you’re free to experiment with different strategies, design intricate railroad networks, and explore the game’s features at your own pace.[/list]

[b]Make sure to leave a review![/b]
We would like to take a moment to t[b]hank all of you for supporting us on this journey.[/b] It means a lot. If you’ve had a chance to play Railroad Corporation 2, we hope you've considered leaving a review with your thoughts! It’s undoubtedly the easiest way to help small developers get their games in front of as many eyes as possible.

[b]We hope you’re as excited as we are for this next step. 
[/b]
Thank you for being part of our community, and we look forward to seeing you on the rails soon.

Corbie Games

notes.title: Railroad Corporation 2: Designing Locomotives
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

We’re back again with another dev log today, and we’ll be covering the core feature in the game: Locomotives in Railroad Corporation 2.

If you've been with us since Railroad Corporation 1, you're likely familiar with the concept: you’ll need to purchase locomotives, each consisting of a single engine, to transport goods and carriages from one city to the next. Initially, only a small handful of locomotive models are available, but as you progress and complete research, new and advanced models unlock for you to add to your arsenal.

Now, in Railroad Corporation 2, we propel ourselves ahead in time, embracing innovations that pave the way for the emergence of new locomotives. As highlighted on the store page, the game primarily unfolds in the early 20th century, an era marked by the advent of electrification, which influenced the locomotives during this time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33938069/bd9c45c10239eab51ea23da912e962f336d6435d.gif[/img]
In Railroad Corporation 2, our aim is to bring realism closer towards Railroad Corporation 2, and the in-game design of locomotives is no exception. Each locomotive model is heavily inspired and crafted based on schematics and properties sourced from reliable online references. Thus, we'd like to provide a walkthrough from schematics to the in-game model, using a locomotive example that we showcased in our last dev log that’ll be featured in Railroad Corporation 2: the 4-8-0 Mastodon steam locomotive!

Firstly, all locomotives within the game are based on design schematics found in online sources or handbooks, which serve as the starting point for the locomotive's design, capturing its details and specifications. Taking the 4-8-0 Mastodon steam locomotive as an example, its design blueprint was drawn from The Norfolk & Western Handbook by Wallace and Wiley, as well as inspired from other online sources.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33938069/15f46db46dff7281e7a3467d6faf3d83d19431a3.png[/img]
[i]Wikimedia Commons - A. Bucher: Das Eisenbahnwesen auf der Weltausstellung in Brüssel 1910. in Polytechnisches Journal, S. 344, Fig. 143[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33938069/033baa363ec7495021302eb4ec3d2419e8cd488a.jpg[/img]
[i]Wikimedia Commons - 1922 Locomotive Cyclopedia of American Practice[/i]

Next, our development team translates the blueprints into a fully realized 3D model, ensuring the dimensions and the core elements are reflected in-game. With the 4-8-0 Mastodon, the visual design of this locomotive is based on the Norfolk and Western M Class, a steam-powered behemoth crafted between 1906 and 1907 by Baldwin Locomotive Works and ALCO-Richmond Works.

Lastly, the technicalities and characteristics are programmed onto each of the locomotives based on their real-life counterpart’s statistics, which reflects how each type of locomotive will behave in-game, which includes details such as train power, tractive effort, maximum speed, locomotive mass, as well as its behavior on road slopes or turn curves, etc.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33938069/5195be56e3eec501987bcd895b1173369d7b97a0.png[/img]
These properties collectively constitute a wealth of information that you must consider when evaluating each locomotive, aiding them in making informed decisions about the most suitable choice for various in-game situations:
[list]
[*] Top speed
[*] Max pulling mass
[*] Acceleration
[*] Reliability rate
[*] Rated mileage
[*] Service life
[*] Fuel conversion efficiency 
[/list]
In addition, there are other technical properties showcased in-game in how locomotives would react to different environments, as well as how each type of carriage would affect the performance of the locomotive in the form of graphic charts comparison.  

For example, the in-game graph below depicts how the nominal speed of a 4-8-0 Mastodon decreases based on both the slope of the terrain it traverses and the weight of its cargo.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33938069/52f335122b8872782535c5c30b255edc0c7f9558.png[/img]

Armed with this information, you can effectively assess which locomotives align with your current requirements. Considerations such as the cargo's weight are essential, as well as factors like the characteristics of the locomotive’s itinerary. Whether you're dealing with short, direct tracks within a local agglomeration or a long-distance route traversing mountains with numerous curves, bridges, and slopes, evaluating locomotives in light of these details becomes crucial for optimal decision-making.

By incorporating these details, we aim to provide you with an immersive experience that stays true to its realism as you navigate the challenges of Railroad Corporation 2. 

And that wraps up today’s dev log. Thanks for your continued support, and stay tuned for more exciting developments as we continue to refine and enhance the world of Railroad Corporation 2!

notes.title: Railroad Corporation: Volatile Markets DLC OUT NOW!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

The economy is a fickle thing -- one day it's up, and the next day it's down. Things were no different in the era of steam engines. That's why we're excited to introduce our new DLC to you: [i]Volatile Markets.[/i]

There's also an update to go along with this DLC, so check out the changelog below as well!

[h2]An all-new challenge[/h2]
A group of rich investors have funded the construction of various plants and factories around the region, and they need your help. You'll be responsible for providing them with crucial resources. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33938069/e153c26e18216d1d1461756fee835e18649e442c.png[/img]

Your railroad corporation will be paid for each delivery you make. However, it is important to remember that it's a free market. Prices for raw materials and finished products are constantly fluctuating, so you will need to plan accordingly, and adapt on the fly. 

[h2]Bring a partner along![/h2]
The Volatile Markets challenge can be played alone, or in co-operative mode. Invite your friend to help you out, as it's always better to have a trustworthy business partner. 

Are you able to thrive in a constantly fluctuating market? Pick up the Volatile Markets DLC and find out!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1568200/Railroad_Corporation__Volatile_Markets_DLC/

notes.title: UPDATE: co-op mode and THREE NEW maps!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

The holidays are coming up, and so here is our gift to you.

[h2]Co-op is here![/h2]
We've been cooking this up for a while now. Co-op is a separate multiplayer mode that puts you and your friend in challenging scenarios where you have no choice but to work together. Support each other in contract work, use each others' railroads, and unite to survive. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33938069/393c0d06708e6e2cbaede7eabc1c2c79fcf30662.png[/img]

[h3]Features:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Work together on the same goals and tasks
[*] Help each other out! When one player loses, the game is over
[*] Contracts can be fulfilled by any player but reward will be received by the one who signed it
[*] No fee charges when using other player’s railroads
[*] Game can be paused during cooperative sessions
[*] Communication during the session is possible via in-game chat
[*] Special co-op scenarios achievements!
[/list]


[h3]Special co-op maps[/h3]
Of course, a new mode is best enjoyed in tailor-made maps. When you boot up co-op mode, you can choose between 3 brand new maps to play with your business partner.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33938069/6f3af185380379bd2e4434c28d88f62901580a41.png[/img]


[b]Shipyard[/b]
The city of Westerly has recently constructed a shipyard. Of course, a shipyard needs ships, and ships need wood. That's what you and your business partner are going to provide!

[b]City prosperity[/b]
Local authorities have issued licenses for rail transport! The condition, however, is that carriers improve development and prosperity in the region. You'll achieve this by providing railroad networks from town to town. 

[b]The Great Partnership[/b]
And of course, there's a sandbox map with no set objectives! You and your partner can explore this large map to your heart's content. 

[h2]Other changes[/h2]
Not into co-op? That's okay! We have some other changes as well, like auto-trading rules that allow you to set up what commodities to buy, sell or move between your factories automatically. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/797400/discussions/0/1741136244272865635/]Check out the changes here.[/url]

Invite a friend and give the new mode a whirl. And of course, let us know what you think on Discord!

notes.title: Signals & Workshop Update Out Now!
notes.content:
[b]We're very excited to share the Signals & Workshop update with you today! In short, signalling directions for track segments and Steam Workshop integration have been added to the game. So, here's what's what, including a big ol' changelog like you're used to from us.
[/b]
[h2]Signal track directions![/h2]
In every mode and mission, it is now possible to change the directions trains can go in, per segment of track. Just click the track icon with the traffic lights in the top right of the screen when playing any mission, map or scenario. Then, click on any segment of the track to change the allowed direction of trains on that section. Single, green arrows signal a one-way track, and blue double arrows signal a two-way track.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33938069/d7cc33e0bd7a727fd028d055da3475d43c72ee3c.gif[/img]

[h2]Create and share via the Editor and Steam Workshop integration[/h2]
Railroad Corporation now has Steam Workshop integration! You can create and share new maps, scenarios and missions for both singleplayer and multiplayer from the editor in the main menu, and you can play community maps, scenarios and missions by subscribing to them from the Steam Workshop hub! Note that the editor has a 'beta' tag on it. That's because the editor might still contain some bugs. If you find any, please let us know in the bug reports section of the Steam forum.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33938069/06af807118f9a1fd77bc35557b7f5bf6e925c4d2.png[/img]

That's not all, check out the full changelog below!

[h3]New features[/h3]
[b]Railroad directions and signals[/b]
To optimize traffic, players are now able to set railroad directions for each segment. Railroad signal poles now reflect the railroad direction setting and prohibit or allow locomotive’s movement. Hold Alt-key to quickly edit directions.

[b]Editor, beta release[/b]
Use Steam Workshop functionality to create, share and play singleplayer and multiplayer maps, missions and scenarios made by the community and yourself.

[b]Train locomotive replacement[/b]
Now a locomotive replacement into a new one can be scheduled in the next train’s waypoint. 

[b]Different resource consumption rates for each city[/b]
Cities can now have different consumption speed, so players may plan which commodity is in higher or lower demand in a certain city.

[b]City population growth rate[/b]
Population growth is affected by fulfilling resource demands in the city hall or local industries. The amount of population growth may differ for individual resources.

[b]UI Top Panel notifications[/b]
Quantity of completed research items is now highlighted with a notification mark in the top panel. A similar notification is shown for new contracts, new staffing availability and new laws.

[b]Commodity selling to a city from your own factories[/b]
It's now possible to prohibit your own production facilities from selling commodities to City Halls.

[b]Using opponents' railroads for pathfinding[/b]
It's now possible to prohibit your locomotives from using the opponent’s railroad while pathfinding.

[h3]Improvements[/h3][list]
[*] Per locomotive lifetime accounting has been added to the train list.
[*] Road length is limited to avoid ineffective cross-map one-click railroad construction.
[*] Couple autosave files have been added to avoid saving right before overdraft or other lose conditions.
[*] Locomotive price of unresearched locomotives is now visible in the characteristics tooltip of the research.
[*] Pathfinding algorithm for locomotives has been optimized.
[*] Overall performance optimization.
[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*] Newly applied routes now stays visible while repairing and refuelling at the station.
[*] Auction panel may duplicate player portraits in some cases. 
[*] Repair action does not reset load/unload actions for the locomotive now. 
[*] Technologies production launch could be delayed for in some cases.
[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33938069/352d751842f6200b452acae52b59d8903b855642.jpg[/img]

Are you of the competitive type, really good at the game or dying to try out multiplayer? Participate in the [b]Railroad Corporation[/b] League!

[h1][b]Information[/b][/h1]
The [b]Railroad Corporation[/b] League (Ladder) is a form of competition where each player is assigned a position (rank). A lower number means a higher rank on the ladder (better position).

The goal of the competition is to move up the Ladder, ultimately to the #1 position (highest rank). Players move up the Ladder (i.e. improve their rank) by winning Ladder games. Players move down the Ladder (i.e. lose their rank) when they lose Ladder games, and when other players move up the Ladder ahead of them.

[h1][b]Rules[/b][/h1]
After each Ladder game has ended, both players are assigned new positions on the Ladder, depending on their current positions, and the result of the game:

1. If the winning player has a lower rank than the losing player, they are moved up half the distance between their position and the losing player's position. The losing player is moved one position down. (For example, if the winning player was 10th and the losing player was 4th on the ladder, their new positions will be 7th ((10+4)/2) and 5th (4+1) after the game)

2. If the winning player is directly below the losing player, their positions are swapped. (i.e. the winning player is moved one position up, and the losing player — one position down)

3. If the winning player has the higher position, they are moved one position up and the losing player is moved one position down.

4. Challenges can only be issued by below player (10 row above is the max. limit)

Hi everyone!

One of the most common concerns we received since the release from players is a time limit set in campaign missions. In this quick patch, No.01, we are [b]tweaking these limits[/b] so players are not pushed too hard to finish the mission fast, but for those who manage to complete tasks fast enough; there's an experience bonus you can earn.

[b]To see these changes, let the game automatically update through Steam and start a new campaign from the main menu. If you're in the middle of a mission now, the next mission will also reflect these changes.[/b]

Of course, there are other critical issues we see and we are working on them already, too. Still, we decided to release this fix to not delay its delivery of what we think will improve gameplay experience right away.

We appreciate all feedback, especially during this Early Access period, and we will take all of your comments and suggestions in consideration to further improve the game.  

We have exciting plans for Railroad Corporation in Early Access and we'll have a roadmap to share, soon!

Thank you for your support!

Love,
The Corbie Games team

notes.title: Relive the Pioneering Spirit of the Golden Age of Steam with 'Railroad Corporation' Coming to PC in 2019

Together with publisher Iceberg Interactive, we are excited to reveal [b]Railroad Corporation[/b], a tycoon strategy game set in 19th century North America during the Golden Age of Steam. The game is slated to launch in early 2019 for PC. Establish your own railroad, build the lines, buy the rolling stock and prosper in the cities you connect - compete against other railroad tycoons and work your way to the top.

https://youtu.be/2HJzfdVOTmA
Begin your career as an ambitious employee of a 19th century railroad company, in the Golden Age of Steam. Manage the business by obeying the directions of your bosses. Build railroads, tunnels and bridges to towns and cities old and new, and decide how to use the railroad to the best advantage of the company. Marvel at the stunningly beautiful scenery that you must blast, dig and tunnel through – nothing must stop the railroad! If you excel, you will get the chance to set up your own railroad corporation, build up the local economy and earn your fortune in the New World. In order to be the very best, you must involve yourself in every aspect of your railroad empire: making new investment decisions, lobbying politicians, managing the global resources of your business empire, and constantly looking over your shoulder at the competition.
